steps.text: Temperature measures how hot an object is; it does not measure the heat it contains.
The zeroth law: two objects in thermal equilibrium with a third are in equilibrium with each other.
Temperature is defined by thermal equilibrium — this is what thermometers exploit.
Heat is energy transferred because of a temperature difference, always hot to cold.
Celsius and kelvin scales have the same step size; 0 K = −273.15 °C.
The kelvin is defined from absolute zero and the triple point of water.
